subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: The Barcode Revolution
description: A 60-second lesson on The Barcode Revolution.

hook.text: The first barcode scanned a pack of Wrigley's gum in 1974. It changed how the world tracks goods.

buildup.text: Before barcodes, inventory was counted by hand. Errors were common and tracking was slow.

discovery.text: Barcodes let machines read product data instantly—at checkout, in warehouses, on shipping docks.

twist.text: The barcode almost died before launch. Grocery stores refused to pay for scanners until volume justified it.

climax.text: Today, over 6 billion barcodes are scanned daily. They're the backbone of modern inventory tracking.

punchline.text: A few black lines unlocked real-time supply chains.

quiz.question: What was the first item to have its barcode scanned?
